questions.question: In linear algebra, what is a vector most generally?
options: Only a column of two real numbers.
A number used to scale other objects.
Only an arrow drawn in the plane.
An element of a vector space.

questions.question: Why can the same vector sometimes be drawn as an arrow and sometimes written as coordinates?
options: Those are different representations of the same kind of object in suitable contexts.
A vector must always be both an arrow and a coordinate list at the same time.
Arrows are used only for complex numbers.
Coordinates are scalars, so they cannot represent vectors.

questions.question: What does a vector in $\mathbb R^n$ have?
options: Exactly two coordinates.
$n$ coordinates.
No coordinate representation.
$n$ different scalar fields.

questions.question: What has to be true before two vectors can be added?
options: They must belong to a vector space where vector addition is defined.
They must be nonzero linear-algebra condition.
They must both be scalars.
They must have different numbers of coordinates, in every case without exception.

questions.question: Is the ordered pair $(2,3)$ automatically treated as a vector or a scalar in $\mathbb R^2$?
options: It is neither a vector nor a coordinate list.
It is a field element of $\mathbb R$.
It is treated as a scalar because it contains numbers.
It is treated as a vector with two coordinates.

questions.question: Which object is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$?
options: $\mathbb R$

questions.question: How many coordinates does $(5,-2,0,7)$ have?
Which vector belongs to $\mathbb R^2$?
If $v=(2,3)$ in $\mathbb R^2$, what is its first coordinate?
Which pair of vectors can be added using ordinary coordinate addition?
options: $\mathbb R^2$ and $(1,0)$

questions.question: Why is it too narrow to define a vector as “an arrow in the plane”?
options: Vectors can never be drawn as arrows.
The plane contains only scalars.
Vectors can also be elements of other vector spaces, such as $\mathbb R^n$ or spaces of matrices.
A vector must always have exactly one coordinate, regardless of the specific input chosen.

questions.question: What is the role of coordinates in describing vectors in $\mathbb R^n$?
options: They replace vector addition by matrix multiplication.
They determine the scalar field automatically as $\mathbb C$.
They make every vector equal to a scalar.
They give an ordered numerical representation of the vector.

questions.question: If $v$ is a vector, what operation with a scalar is expected in a vector space?
options: Division by every other vector.
Changing the field into a vector, no matter which values are selected.
Taking a determinant of $v$.
Scalar multiplication, producing another vector.

questions.question: Which statement correctly classifies $(1,0,-4)$?
options: It is a vector in $\mathbb R^3$.
It is a vector in $\mathbb R^2$.
It is a scalar in $\mathbb R$.
It is the field $\mathbb R^3$.

questions.question: If a vector has six real coordinates, in which coordinate space is it naturally placed?
options: $\mathbb R$ only
$\mathbb R^6$
$\mathbb R^2$
$\mathbb C$

questions.question: Which expression is a vector operation rather than a scalar alone?
options: $3\cdot 2$

questions.question: Can the same coordinate list represent different mathematical objects in different settings?
options: No, coordinate lists are always scalars.
No, every coordinate list has one universal meaning.
Yes, but only if all coordinates are zero.
Yes, its meaning depends on the ambient space and context.

questions.question: Why does the phrase “$v$ is a vector” usually leave some context implicit?
options: One should know only whether $v$ is positive.
No context is ever needed for vectors.
One should know the determinant of $v$.
One should know which vector space $v$ belongs to.

questions.question: Which vector is not in $\mathbb R^3$?
If $u=(1,2,3)$ and $v=(4,5)$, what is the problem with adding $u+v$ as vectors in coordinate spaces?
options: The first vector has no coordinates.
Both vectors are zero.
Addition is never allowed for vectors.
They have different numbers of coordinates.
